title: Verifier-Guided Repair of LLM-Generated Vendor CLI Configurations: A Controlled Fault-Injection Paired Study
abstract: We evaluate whether exposing deterministic verifier diagnostics to an LLM-based repair workflow reduces residual unsafe or invalid vendor-CLI configurations compared with blind repair. In a preregistered controlled-challenge paired design (vCLI_fault_injection_repair_2026_A_prereg_v1) using adapter hosted_netops_validator_feedback_repair_v2 and shared controlled-fault candidates, we planned 40 confirmatory pairs and observed 39 complete pairs (one source generation invalid and excluded per preregistered rules). Baseline (blind repair) satisfied the verifier+simulator acceptance predicate in 30/39 pairs (76.92%); guarded (verifier-guided) satisfied it in 38/39 pairs (97.44%). Paired counts: n11 = 29, n10 = 9 (guarded-only), n01 = 1 (baseline-only), n00 = 0. The paired absolute difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.20512820512820507 (20.51 percentage points); two-sided exact paired test p = 0.021484375; 95% paired-bootstrap percentile CI = [0.07692307692307693, 0.358974358974359] (bootstrap resamples = 10000, seed = 1729). Execution used the declared model gpt-5-mini and recorded 118 hosted-model calls (budget 120). A preregistered confirmatory harmful-overrepair aggregation was not produced by the archived confirmatory executor; we provide the precise archived artifact locations and the compact harmful-change mapping required to reproduce that preregistered safety aggregation and treat that safety verdict as unresolved in the confirmatory summary.

sections.introduction:
Generative large language models (LLMs) are increasingly proposed as aides in network operations (NetOps) for tasks such as intent-to-configuration translation and automated remediation. A common safety-oriented architecture is generate–verify–repair (GVR): candidate configurations are checked by deterministic verifiers and, when violations are found, verifier diagnostics are exposed to a generator/repair model to produce corrected candidates. Prior empirical work in code and Infrastructure-as-Code (IaC) settings reports that verifier-interposed repair can raise verifier-detected pass rates while exposing new failure modes (e.g., verifier-exploitation) and imposing interaction costs [1], [2], [3], [4]. Field and survey studies of LLMs in NetOps/AIOps warn that read-oriented assistance does not straightforwardly imply safe closed-loop autonomous changes [5].

Motivation and research question. Controlled paired evidence on verifier-guided repair applied to vendor command-line interface (CLI) templates with preregistered realistic fault operators is sparse. A core methodological concern is intervention informativeness: a verifier-guided repair can affect outcomes only when initial candidates trigger actionable diagnostics. We address that concern with a preregistered deterministic controlled-fault injection and a paired shared-candidate design (preregistered estimator: paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline). Research question: Does exposing deterministic verifier diagnostics to an LLM repair workflow reduce residual unsafe or invalid vendor-CLI configurations compared with blind repair when confronted with preregistered controlled faults?
sections.related_work: Empirical and methodological work on GVR-style pipelines establishes both promise and caveats. Work describing generate–verify–repair architectures and controlled evaluations in code and IaC domains finds deterministic verifiers can materially raise verifier-detected pass rates and that supplying verifier diagnostics to a repair model improves recheck success rates [1], [2]. Controlled analyses demonstrate a concrete exploitation risk: optimizing toward a single verifier proxy can produce pathological degradations of the true target property in iterative-refinement contexts [3]. Other studies quantify the interaction costs of verifier-mediated pipelines (a "verifier tax") and emphasize tradeoffs between safety gains and increased interaction horizons and resource use [4]. Surveys and field case studies in NetOps/AIOps show broad usefulness for read-oriented assistance but emphasize that safe closed-loop execution requires strong verification, conservative orchestration, and domain-grounded evaluation [5]. These verified prior findings motivated (a) a deterministic controlled-challenge paired design to ensure intervention activation, (b) shared controlled-fault candidate semantics for a clear causal estimand, and (c) preregistered harmful-change rules and missingness policies to support auditable safety aggregation.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and estimand. The study was preregistered as vCLI_fault_injection_repair_2026_A_prereg_v1. The primary estimand is the paired difference in the combined verifier+simulator pass indicator (paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline). The preregistration SHA-256 is recorded in the execution manifest (preregistration_sha256 = 0ba66573928647f008b2cd5b9dde6708a61ae86ece55b693ace534e01e2b132c).

Design and adapter semantics. Confirmatory execution used adapter hosted_netops_validator_feedback_repair_v2 under its shared_controlled_fault_candidate semantics: for each preregistered task index a single deterministic controlled-fault candidate (deterministic_netops_fault_injector_v1) was produced and reused across both conditions. Each pair received exactly one initial generation (shared) and one repair opportunity per condition; baseline denotes blind repair (no diagnostics exposed) and guarded denotes repair with deterministic validator diagnostics exposed. The adapter-mandated confirmatory task_count was fixed at 40; execution completed 39 valid pairs (see Results).

Models, sampling records, and determinism. The archived model configuration declares declared_model_version = gpt-5-mini and records temperature = null/unset in execution/model_configuration.json. Null/unset is not evidence of deterministic sampling and does not imply temperature = 0. Runtime sampling parameters and per-call metadata required to assess sampling behavior are archived and available per model call: see execution/provider_calls/ (per-episode provider traces), execution/execution_log.jsonl (call-level timestamps and terminal statuses), and execution/model_configuration.json (declared settings). Auditors can inspect those artifacts to reconstruct actual runtime sampling parameters for each hosted-model call. Exactly one sampled initial generation per task pair was performed and reused by both arms under the shared_controlled_fault_candidate semantics as recorded in the execution manifest.

Controlled-challenge sampling and informativeness. To ensure intervention activation, the confirmatory design used deterministic controlled faults (task indices 1..40) that inject realistic actionable violations (examples: dropped_required_restore, protected_interface_change, atomic MTU-change patterns). The execution manifest records controlled_fault_assignment_sha256 = 8d0879...75c6 and source_generation_attempt_count = 40 (source_valid_count = 39, source_invalid_or_failed_count = 1). The preregistered missingness rule 'complete_pair_primary' excludes a pair only if both condition executions are unscorable; that exclusion occurred once and is documented in analysis/missingness_summary.csv.

Scoring, harmful-change mapping, and analysis plan. The primary success predicate required both the deterministic vendor-CLI validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) and simulator-based compliance agreement. The preregistration specified a harmful-change labeling schema to support a confirmatory harmful-overrepair hypothesis; the compact operational mapping archived with the transformation artifacts labels an episode harmful if validation_after.violation_codes contains PROTECTED_INTERFACE_CHANGE or UNINTENDED_STATE_CHANGE. The primary statistical test was a two-sided exact paired binary test (McNemar exact or equivalent), reporting discordant counts, absolute risk difference, two-sided exact p-value, and a 95% paired-bootstrap percentile CI (bootstrap resamples = 10000, seed = 1729). Missingness sensitivity analyses were preregistered (primary exclusion rule and alternative sensitivity treating missing as failure). All per-episode traces and transformation artifacts required to reproduce primary and preregistered secondary statistics are archived (execution/raw_results.jsonl; execution/scoring/*.json; execution/transformation_manifest.json).
sections.results:
Execution accounting. Planned confirmatory pairs = 40; completed episodes = 78 (39 complete pairs) with failed_episode_count = 2. Hosted-model calls used = 118 (<= planned maximum 120). Source-generation attempts = 40 (source_valid_count = 39; source_invalid_or_failed_count = 1). Run timestamps are recorded in the execution manifest (started_at_utc = 2026-09-04T21:16:50.730326+00:00; completed_at_utc = 2026-09-04T21:19:34.370550+00:00). Key archived artifacts: execution/raw_results.jsonl, execution/scoring/*.json, analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv, analysis/condition_summary.csv, and execution/model_configuration.json (paths and artifact hashes are recorded in the execution manifest).

Primary confirmatory outcomes (complete_pairs = 39). Baseline (blind repair) success = 30/39 = 0.7692307692307693. Guarded (verifier-guided) success = 38/39 = 0.9743589743589743. Paired contingency counts (guarded, baseline): n11 = 29, n10 = 9 (guarded-only), n01 = 1 (baseline-only), n00 = 0. Paired estimate (guarded − baseline) = 0.20512820512820507 (20.51 percentage points). Exact two-sided paired test (McNemar exact): p = 0.021484375. 95% paired-bootstrap percentile CI = [0.07692307692307693, 0.358974358974359] (bootstrap_resamples = 10000, bootstrap_seed = 1729). The archived condition summary and paired table are available at analysis/condition_summary.csv and analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv with recorded artifact hashes.

Missingness and exclusions. One pair was excluded under the preregistered 'complete_pair_primary' rule because its source-generation was invalid/unscorable (both_missing_pairs = 1; source_invalid_or_failed_count = 1). The per-episode terminal error reasons are archived in execution/execution_log.jsonl and execution/raw_results.jsonl for audit.

Preregistered harmful-overrepair aggregation: status and reproducibility path. The preregistration included a confirmatory test that guarded repair would not increase harmful over-repair beyond a prespecified threshold. The archived confirmatory analysis executor produced the primary paired result but did not compute the preregistered harmful-overrepair aggregation (secondary_results = []). Because the preregistered harmful-overrepair aggregation was not produced in the archived confirmatory summary, we do not assert a confirmatory safety verdict here. To reproduce the preregistered harmful-overrepair aggregation exactly as preregistered, auditors must: (1) iterate the complete pairs (analysis/missingness_summary.csv shows complete_pairs = 39), (2) for each episode read validation_after.violation_codes from execution/scoring/<episode>.json (or execution/raw_results.jsonl), (3) label episode harmful if the validation_after.violation_codes set contains PROTECTED_INTERFACE_CHANGE or UNINTENDED_STATE_CHANGE (the compact mapping archived at execution/transformation_manifest.json), and (4) compute paired harmful counts and the paired difference per the preregistered analysis plan. All per-episode fields and the transformation artifact implementing the mapping are present in the archive; the archived confirmatory executor did not run this aggregation and therefore the preregistered confirmatory safety verdict remains unresolved in this manuscript.

Representative diagnostics. Representative per-pair scoring artifacts are archived (execution/scoring/task-000001-*.json, task-000002-*.json, task-000003-*.json). Example: pair-000003 shows a protected-interface-change fault where baseline repair left PROTECTED_INTERFACE_CHANGE violations while guarded repair removed those violations and produced a valid configuration. These per-episode traces support a mechanistic account in which diagnostics direct targeted corrective edits.
sections.discussion:
Interpretation and mechanism. The preregistered paired result indicates that exposing deterministic verifier diagnostics to the repair model substantially increases verifier+simulator-validated post-repair success on this controlled synthetic task bank (approx. +20.51 percentage points). The shared-candidate paired semantics isolate the effect of exposing diagnostics because both arms received the identical initial controlled-fault candidate and identical repair budgets. Per-episode validator traces show diagnostics frequently identify concrete protected fields or missing restore steps; furnishing these diagnostics to the model appears to produce targeted edits that remove verifier-detected violations (supporting a plausible causal pathway from diagnostic exposure to improved verified outcomes without requiring additional independent first-pass generations).

Safety boundary and unresolved preregistered safety aggregation. We emphasize that the preregistered confirmatory harmful-overrepair aggregation was not produced by the archived confirmatory executor and therefore remains unresolved for the confirmatory claim. The compact harmful-change mapping and per-episode traces needed for that aggregation are archived and their exact artifact locations are documented above and in the execution manifest; independent auditors can compute the preregistered safety statistic deterministically from those artifacts. We treat exploratory reconstructions produced outside the archived confirmatory summary as exploratory only.

Operational implications and verifier tax. The verifier-guided workflow imposes measurable interaction steps: the execution manifest records hosted_model_call_event_count = 118 and stage_counts enumerating source generation and both repair stages. These counts permit exploratory computations such as model-call cost per avoided failure, but the present confirmatory experiment was not sized to generalize operational cost/latency tradeoffs to production. Practitioners should budget for verifier-mediated call counts and instrument both verifier coverage and harmful-change indicators before closed-loop deployment.

Verifier-exploitation and generality. Prior work documents verifier-exploitation risk when optimizing against a single proxy verifier in long-horizon iterative pipelines [3]. Our short repair budget and shared-candidate pairing reduce exposure to long-horizon exploitation but do not eliminate it; multi-verifier ensembles, enforced harmful-change constraints, calibrated abstention, and explicit uncertainty quantification remain recommended mitigations. External validity is limited: execution used a single declared model (gpt-5-mini) and a synthetic controlled-fault bank; replication across diverse models, verifiers, and naturalistic NetOps workloads is required.
sections.conclusion:
In a preregistered controlled-challenge paired experiment using hosted_netops_validator_feedback_repair_v2 and shared controlled-fault candidates, exposing deterministic verifier diagnostics to an LLM repair workflow produced a statistically detectable and substantial increase in verifier+simulator-validated configuration success (approx. +20.51 percentage points; p = 0.021484375; 95% CI [0.07692307692307693, 0.358974358974359]). This finding is bounded to the preregistered synthetic task bank, the declared model (gpt-5-mini), and the archived deterministic verifier and simulator. The preregistered confirmatory harmful-overrepair aggregation was not present in the archived confirmatory summary and therefore remains unresolved here; the archived artifacts and transformation manifest provide the exact inputs for independent recomputation of that preregistered statistic. We release the evidence bundle for reproducible reaggregation and recommend multi-model and multi-verifier replications together with larger-scale cost/latency studies to assess operational feasibility and safety at NetOps scale.

References

[1] R. Cadenas, "Convergent Correctness in Stochastic Code Generation: A Generate-Verify-Repair Architecture for Deterministic Validation of Autonomous AI Coding Agents in Regulated Environments," SSRN, 2026. doi:10.2139/ssrn.6754899.

[2] M. Jouini, "Verifier-First Evaluation of Agentic LLMs for Infrastructure-as-Code Generation," arXiv:2607.20478, 2026.

[3] A. Gupta, "Verifier Exploitation in NLI-Guided Iterative Refinement: A Controlled Empirical Analysis," Research Square, 2026. doi:10.21203/rs.3.rs-10187492/v1.

[4] T. Sah, V. Srivastava, D. Sah, and K. Jordan, "The Verifier Tax: Horizon Dependent Safety Success Tradeoffs in Tool Using LLM Agents," arXiv:2603.19328, 2026.

[5] M. Bilal, J. Crowcroft, R. Wang, X. Xu, and S. Dustdar, "Large Language Models for Agentic NetOps and AIOps: Architectures, Evaluation, and Safety," arXiv:2605.12729, 2026.

Execution semantics: execution/model_configuration.json records temperature = null/unset; null/unset is not evidence of deterministic sampling and does not imply temperature = 0. limitations: Synthetic controlled-fault task bank: tasks were deterministically injected and do not represent a broad naturalistic distribution of production NetOps incidents; external validity to live operator workloads is limited.
Single-model and single-adapter evaluation: confirmatory execution used only the declared model gpt-5-mini and one adapter family; results do not establish multi-model generality.
Simulator-backed primary success predicate: primary success required agreement of deterministic verifier and simulator; simulator fidelity and verifier coverage constrain construct validity.

Sample size and power: complete_pairs = 39 provides detectable effects of the observed magnitude but limits precision for subgroup and per-fault-class inference; exploratory subgroup analyses are not confirmatory.
Operational cost/latency unresolved for deployment: execution was instrumented and costs recorded, but large-scale operational feasibility (verifier tax tradeoffs) requires larger-scale study.

Verifier-exploitation and long-horizon agentic pathologies remain possible: this controlled setting mitigates some risks, but broader agentic workflows need additional defenses (multi-verifier designs, calibrated abstention, uncertainty quantification).

Preregistered confirmatory harmful-overrepair test not present in archived confirmatory summary: the archived confirmatory analysis executor did not compute the preregistered harmful-overrepair aggregation; the required per-episode traces and transformation manifest are archived and available for independent reaggregation, but the preregistered confirmatory safety verdict is therefore unresolved in this paper.
